Mixing Cannabis Drinks: What You Need to Know

Mixing cannabis beverages with alcohol can significantly amplify impairment and unpredictably alter subjective effects, which is why combining substances is generally discouraged from a harm-reduction standpoint. Alcohol may increase cannabinoid absorption and affect cognitive and motor functions more profoundly than either substance alone, and certain medications can interact with cannabinoids in clinically significant ways. If you are considering combining products, please do so only with a clear and informed awareness of dosing, and always consult healthcare providers when taking prescription medications that may interact with cannabinoids. Safer alternatives include staggered consumption with long waiting intervals or thoughtfully choosing alcohol-free mixers to avoid compounding impairment.

Consumer Preferences for CBD and THC Infused Beverages

Cannabis regulatory reform has opened areas for product innovation and entrepreneurship. One dimension that has so far been understudied is the potential for cannabidiol (CBD) and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) beverages. This study uses double-bounded contingent valuation techniques and parametric and nonparametric estimation procedures to assess consumer demand and willingness to pay (WTP) for various cannabis-infused beverages. By targeting a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults, the study finds that roughly half of consumers are willing to try cannabis-infused beverages. Among these respondents, cannabis-infused juices and sweetened iced tea elicit the highest mean WTP, though the WTP for other beverage options varies across demographics and consumer preferences. On average, the mean WTP for THC-infused beverages is 12.5% higher per 12 oz can than its CBD-infused counterpart, and younger consumers are willing to pay more for each of these products.

THC/CBD Spray Pharmacokinetics and Safety Study

Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol and CBD were rapidly absorbed following single-dose administration. With increasing single and multiple doses of THC/CBD spray, the mean peak plasma concentration (Cmax) increased for all analytes. There was evidence of dose-proportionality in the single but not the multiple dosing data sets. The bioavailability of THC was greater than CBD at single and multiple doses, and there was no evidence of accumulation for any analyte with multiple dosing. Inter-subject variability ranged from moderate to high for all PK parameters in this study. The time to peak plasma concentration (Tmax) was longest for all analytes in the eight spray group, but was similar in the two and four spray groups. THC/CBD spray was well-tolerated in this study and no serious adverse events were reported. The mean Cmaxvalues (<12 ng/mL) recorded in this study were well below those reported in patients who smoked/inhaled cannabis, which is reassuring since elevated Cmaxvalues are linked to significant psychoactivity. There was also no evidence of accumulation on repeated dosing.

Frequently Asked Questions About Cannabis Beverages

When selecting your ideal cannabis beverage, thoughtfully consider factors such as the specific type of cannabinoid (THC or CBD), your desired effects, and the beverage’s delightful flavor profile. Potential side effects of cannabis beverages can include mild dizziness, an increased heart rate, feelings of anxiety, and impaired coordination, especially if consumed in higher doses. Individual reactions naturally vary based on factors like your personal tolerance, metabolism, and the specific formulation of the beverage. It’s essential to carefully monitor your body’s unique response and adjust your consumption accordingly. If you experience any severe side effects, such as extreme anxiety or confusion, please seek a calm environment and hydrate until the effects gently subside.

Yes, cannabis beverages can indeed be considered for pain management, particularly those thoughtfully infused with CBD, which is widely recognized for its anti-inflammatory properties. However, it’s crucial to consult with a trusted healthcare professional before using cannabis for pain management, especially if you are currently taking other medications or have underlying health conditions. Always start with low doses to accurately assess effectiveness and your personal tolerance.

To maintain the exquisite quality and potency of your cannabis beverages, store them in a cool, dark place, safely away from direct sunlight and heat. Refrigeration is often highly recommended, especially for beverages that contain perishable ingredients. Always check the product label for specific storage instructions, as some drinks may have different requirements.
